meta.name: nepali-finetune-plan
meta.note: Investigation plan for language adaptation + speaker adaptation. No training is started by this file.
meta.currentAppArchitecture: Fish Audio CLOUD API only — no local fish-speech Python install in this repo

A_cloud_language_ft.evidence: OpenAPI POST /model train_mode is const 'fast' only; no LoRA/full/language fine-tune endpoint in api.fish.audio OpenAPI

B_better_fast_clone.evidence: voices[] 1-20 + texts[] exact Devanagari; speaker conditioning only — not deep language FT

C_current_product_cloud_ft.note: Language fine-tuning not exposed on public cloud API used by this app

D_base_model_limiter.evidence: No language field; no Nepali pronunciation_dictionary; opaque s2.1-pro-free; must A/B vs Gemini ne-NP to quantify

determination.summary: Primary: Case C (no cloud language FT). Secondary risk: strong Case D (model Nepali quality). Best free path: Case B multi-sample re-record + listen A/B.

whatExists: Voice cloning via POST https://api.fish.audio/model with voices[] + texts[] + tags + train_mode=fast
Optional zero-shot references[] on /v1/tts (MessagePack) — separate from clone
whatIsUnknownFromRepo: Enterprise/custom checkpoint training not documented in public OpenAPI — assume unavailable unless Fish support confirms
actionRequired: No public language FT — do not wait on cloud FT to improve quality
Use multi-sample fast clone + reference script instead

pathB_open_fish_speech_local.reason: This project has ZERO local fish-speech runtime (no .py, no checkpoint, no GPU training loop). Local FT would be a NEW subsystem, not a patch.

ifPursuedLater.typicalMethod: Fine-tune text-to-speech LLM / codec tokens on parallel (audio, transcript) pairs; speaker via reference tokens or speaker embedding
ifPursuedLater.languageAdaptation: Include large Nepali corpus so tokenizer+acoustic path learns Devanagari→sound
ifPursuedLater.speakerPreservation: Freeze or lightly adapt speaker encoder; mix original speaker data with Nepali text if multi-speaker; or train speaker adapter after language FT
ifPursuedLater.loRA: Common on transformer LM backbone of fish-speech-class models — lower VRAM, less speaker damage risk than full FT
ifPursuedLater.fullFT: Highest quality language shift; higher risk of catastrophic speaker drift without speaker data mix

minDatasetRough.languageAdaptationOnly: 10–100+ hours clean Nepali (multi-speaker preferred) beyond single-voice clone
minDatasetRough.singleSpeakerCloneStyle: 0.5–10 minutes already used for zero-shot clone; insufficient alone for deep language FT
minDatasetRough.recommendedStartingPoint: 5–20 hours single-speaker high-quality Nepali for joint speaker+language; 50+ hours multi-speaker for robust ne-TTS

ifPursuedLater.audioFormat: 16-bit PCM WAV preferred; 16 kHz minimum, 22.05/24/44.1 kHz common
ifPursuedLater.transcripts: UTF-8 Devanagari, sentence-aligned, one speaker, no music
ifPursuedLater.segmentation: 0.5–15 s utterances typical; no long silences mid-phrase

paramsRough.steps: tens of thousands for full FT; fewer for LoRA
paramsRough.vram: LoRA often 12–24 GB class; full FT may need 24–80 GB depending on model size — VERIFY against installed fish-speech version docs
paramsRough.risk: speaker similarity drop if Nepali FT data is a different speaker than target clone

pathC_alternative_nepali_tts.purpose: Phase 12 — answer whether Fish is the limiter without destroying current system

speakerIdentityProtocol.before: Generate reference sentence list with current clone
compare: speaker similarity (human or embedding if available)
speakerIdentityProtocol.failCondition: Pronunciation improves but speaker identity significantly deteriorates → do not ship

decisionGate: 1. Cloud language FT: CLOSED (Case C) — no public endpoint
2. Improve multi-sample clone (Case B) + listen A/B for Case D magnitude
3. If Case D dominates: pathB local FT as separate module OR pathC alternative engine
4. Never auto-start training from this app
